v.why: Raising an already large learning rate causes divergence, as in experiments 7 and 10.
Lowering a very large learning rate restores stable training, with big gains in experiments 8, 15 and 17.
At tiny learning rates the model is undertrained in 243 epochs, so a larger rate helps, as in experiment 1.
Deeper nets are less stable at high learning rates, with large drops in experiments 87 and 97.
Shallower nets tolerate large learning rates better, as in experiment 99.
Stronger L2 penalty on an already heavily regularized net causes underfitting, as in experiments 64 and 78.
Relaxing excessive regularization recovers accuracy, as in experiments 62, 68 and 73.
With tiny learning rates, wider layers learn faster and so help, as in experiment 49.
A single-hidden-layer net has little spare capacity, so more L2 hurts, as in experiments 64, 67, 72 and 78.
Deeper nets with strong L2 shrink toward trivial solutions, as in experiment 84.

raw:
Most of these come from the lr-heavy patterns in the experiments. Large learning rates paired with a step up in lr or depth collapse accuracy, while stepping lr down from a high value helps. Strong L2 penalties are hurt by a further increase. The width and depth-1 alpha hypotheses are weaker and rest on only a few experiments.
